key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved solar-cell efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against environmental degradation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, ambient-stable hybrid silicon photovoltaics on untextured substrates.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer cells against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si references.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and conductivity enhancement.
Insert graphene as a charge-transport interface and protective barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for pristine graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 ambient-exposure days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The 75-day ambient test does not establish long-term outdoor durability or manufacturing-scale barrier integrity.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
